_comments: The BizApps Contracts Application — what makes this app appear in MJ Explorer at all.
WITHOUT THIS FILE the app is invisible. CodeGen auto-creates a schema-named application
(__mj_BizAppsContracts) that carries the entities, but that is a container for admin access, not a
destination: no nav items, no icon, so nobody finds the app by looking. This row is the
user-facing app.
DefaultNavItems IS the top nav bar. Each item is ResourceType 'Custom' pointing at a DriverClass
registered via @RegisterClass(BaseResourceComponent, '<DriverClass>') in @mj-biz-apps/contracts-ng.
BOTH HALVES ARE REQUIRED: metadata without a registered class renders a dead tab, and a registered
class without metadata never appears.
THREE SECTIONS, ruled 2026-08-18. Each owns a LEFT RAIL over its own sub-pages — MJ's rule is top
nav ACROSS sections, left nav WITHIN one:
Contracts     — Dashboard · All Contracts · Renewals & Expiry · Awaiting Documents · Modifications
Templates     — Agreement Versions · All Provisions
Configuration — Contract Types · Template Types · Reference Data
WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT V1'S. v1's three were Contracts / Billing / Setup, and Billing was a peer
because 'what failed to bill and why' is a different job done by different people. The rebuild
deleted billing entirely, so that section had nothing behind it. Templates earns the vacated slot
for the same reason Billing did: registering the next Master Agreement version and curating its
clause list is finance-adjacent legal work, done rarely, by someone who is not filing contracts
that day. Filing it under Contracts would bury the one surface that has to be findable before a
modification can be recorded at all (item 4 is a prerequisite, not a nicety).
Modifications is a RAIL TAB under Contracts, not a section: 'every deviation we have ever agreed
to' is a way of reading contracts, not a separate job. Awaiting Documents is a rail tab for the
same reason — it is the IsAwaitingDocument filter over the same list, which is exactly why that
column is derived in the base view rather than being a stored worklist flag.
DefaultForNewUser is true so the app lands for new users without a per-persona grant. When it is
false you must run `mjdev apps enable <slug> <app>` or the app stays hidden even though everything
is installed correctly — a confusing failure that looks like a build problem.
The fixed UUID means a re-push against a rebuilt database UPDATES this row rather than creating a
second Application with the same name. Unchanged from v1 deliberately: it is the same app.

fields.Name: Contracts
fields.Description: The record of what we agreed: every agreement, the standard terms it incorporates, the provisions negotiated away from those terms, and the executed paper. Contracts tracks obligations and documents; orders bills, and sales sells.
